featured_videos.title: The BEST Zero Carb Wrap!
featured_videos.creator: Keto Rewind
featured_videos.commentary: The community's response here is really telling, and it's not just about the wrap. People are celebrating Jess for being real about the journey, not perfect. That "getting back on the horse" comment hits different because it's exactly what most of us need to hear, especially when we're on vacation and the pressure to stay strict feels heavy. The wrap itself is clever, but what's resonating is the permission she's giving everyone to enjoy food without spiraling, which honestly matters more than any zero-carb hack. That's the vibe that keeps people coming back.

featured_videos.title: ARMY VET UNDER ATTACK FOR LOSING 130 POUNDS
featured_videos.creator: Russell Does Stuff
featured_videos.editorial_title: ARMY VET UNDER ATTACK FOR LOSING 130 POUNDS
featured_videos.commentary: There's a real pattern here that matters beyond the drama. When someone loses 130 pounds and shares how they did it, the immediate attack isn't usually about the science. It's about control over the narrative. What strikes me is that the comments defending the veteran focus on something simple: he never told anyone they *had* to do carnivore. He just showed his results and his bloodwork. That's not misinformation, that's just a person talking about their own experience. The pushback gets intense precisely because it works for some people, and that contradicts what people are being told should work. Whether it's carnivore, keto, or any diet that breaks from mainstream messaging, there's this reflexive need to tear it down rather than just let it exist as one option among many.

featured_videos.title: People Need To Pay Attention To What This 85 Year Old Carnivore Is Doing!
featured_videos.creator: Shawn Baker MD
featured_videos.editorial_title: People Need To Pay Attention To What This 85 Year Old Carnivore Is Doing!
featured_videos.commentary: What strikes me most isn't just that she's 85 and lifting weights, it's that the comments keep mentioning the same thing: attitude, activity, time outside, independence. The people in this thread aren't just celebrating her physique (though yeah, she looks incredible for 85). They're pointing to something bigger. That one comment about "it's not just what you eat, it is how you live" got me because it's true. Carnivore gives you the metabolic foundation, but what she's doing with that foundation. staying active, staying connected, staying purposeful. that's what's actually keeping her young. This is exactly why I wrote about aging on carnivore the way I did. The diet works, but only if you use it as a tool for living harder, not just living longer.

featured_videos.title: Sunscreen causes cancer?  Another carnivore lie debunked.
featured_videos.creator: Haircafe
featured_videos.editorial_title: Sunscreen causes cancer?  Another carnivore lie debunked.
featured_videos.commentary: The sunscreen debate is blowing up everywhere right now, and honestly, it's a perfect example of how the carnivore community gets painted with the wrong brush. Haircafe does a solid job here breaking down the actual science instead of letting fear-mongering win, which matters because your friends mocking you for daily sunscreen? They're operating on a viral claim, not evidence. The real move isn't choosing between "sunscreen causes cancer" or "ignore the sun entirely" - it's understanding UV damage is real, sunscreen works, and you don't have to pick between carnivore and basic skin protection. That one comment about animals using their own defenses (fur, staying out of peak sun, behavioral adaptation) actually nails it - we're not evolved for Australian midday UV like our ancestors weren't either.
